hook_text: The clinic ramp is 1 in 6. Push a loaded wheelbarrow up it and you will understand the rule in two seconds.
clip_script: Walk through town with a tape measure. The Spar ramp: 450 up over 5 400, 1 in 12, passes. The clinic: 600 over 3 600, 1 in 6, a slide. The school ramp bolted on twenty years late: steel, rusting, no landing, so the chair user holds the door with one hand and the rail with the other. Concrete lasts but is slow. Steel is quick but rusts. Timber is nice to hold but rots. Look for hazards: odd steps, missing rails, no kerb, puddles. Guess the cost from the materials. Then write the table: what you saw, what the standard says, what it teaches you. Every line becomes a rule in your own brief.
visual_style: Whiteboard town street with four entrances sketched; a gradient calculation beside each; a three-column table filling with ticks, crosses and lessons.
pacing: Four entrances fast, materials, hazards, cost, the table.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and measure the gradient of one ramp near you.
